The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the conveyor belt is μ. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a small block is placed on a horizontal conveyor belt. The block is connected to a fixed point above by a thin rope inclined upward to the right; beside the upper surface of the conveyor belt there is a velocity arrow pointing to the left, indicating that the conveyor belt at the contact point with the block moves to the left. Reasoning: The block is tied by the thin rope and remains stationary relative to the ground, while the conveyor belt moves to the left, so the block slides relative to the conveyor belt and is subjected to kinetic friction exerted by the conveyor belt to the left. Let the angle between the thin rope and the horizontal direction be θ, and the tension in the rope be T. When the block is in equilibrium, in the horizontal direction there is T cosθ = f = μN; in the vertical direction there is N + T sinθ = mg. Substituting N = mg - T sinθ gives T cosθ = μ(mg - T sinθ), that is, T(cosθ + μ sinθ)=μmg, so T = μmg/(cosθ + μ sinθ). This expression is only related to m, μ, and the angle θ of the rope, and is unrelated to the magnitude v of the conveyor belt speed. Therefore, when the conveyor belt moves at v1 and v2 respectively, as long as relative sliding occurs in both cases, the tension in the rope is the same.
